newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Rights group members says police beat E.Timorese.
newsitem.headline: Rights group members says police beat E.Timorese.

text.p: A member of Indonesia's National Human Rights Commission on Saturday accused police of maltreating East Timorese protesters during a visit by U.N. special envoy Jamsheed Marker this week.

"It's obvious the protesters have been beaten. They have swollen eyes, mouths, backs and chests. Some haven't eaten for four days because they can't do it as the result of the beating," commission member Clementino Dos Reis Amaral, a native of East Timor, told Reuters by telephone.

East Timor deputy police chief Lieutenant-Colonel Atok Rismanto said police sought only to disperse the protesters. "What police did was dispersing the protesters ... not killing them," he said from Dili, capital of East Timor, without giving other details.

Amaral, who visited East Timor with colleague Albert Hasibuan this week, was referring to 24 East Timorese who were arrested on charges of publicly showing hatred against the Indonesian government during Sunday's protest in the lobby of Mahkota hotel in Dili where Marker was staying.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.

"There is an evidence the 24 people have experienced some kind of torture. Police attacked the protesters with sticks and also kicked and punched them," said Amaral, adding that the suspects were held at the Becora prison in Dili.

He said 11 other East Timorese were still being treated at a military hospital after a clash with police who tried to quell the protest. He added two other women were also detained at the police station.
"The two women were beaten ... Their eyes are swollen," Amaral said. "In total, we have found out there are 37 protesters who have been injured during the protest."
Amaral said he and his colleage met the detainees, adding their visit to East Timor, which lasted from Tuesday to Thursday, was a routine one. The Human Rights Commission has an office in Dili.
Hasibuan was not available for comment on Saturday, but the Jakarta Post newspaper quoted him as saying authorities should not have taken the law into their hands.
Marker, who flew back to Jakarta on Monday after a three-day visit in East Timor, said he was in his room at the time of the demonstration and did not see what happened.
Residents said demonstrators tried to meet Marker after they felt frustrated that he was meeting only government officials and Nobel Peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo.
Marker denied he had refused to meet the students, saying they had not asked for a meeting.
